hook.text: Finding friends-of-friends in a relational database requires expensive recursive JOINs. Graphs do it in milliseconds.

buildup.text: Graph databases like Neo4j store data as nodes and edges, optimized for relationship traversal.

discovery.text: Querying 'friends who also like jazz' traverses edges directly instead of joining large tables.

twist.text: Graphs struggle with simple aggregations like counting or summing. Not every query is a traversal.

climax.text: Graph databases excel at social networks, recommendations, and fraud detection — anywhere relationships matter.

punchline.text: When relationships are the data, use a graph database.

quiz.question: When are graph databases most useful?
options: When queries involve traversing relationships between entities
